title: BABA: Valuation Re-evaluated (Narrow Moat)

AI-related product revenue achieved its 12th consecutive quarter of triple-digit growth, reaching an annualized run-rate of $7.3 billion (RMB 49.5 billion) and accounting for 35% of external cloud revenue, while Model-as-a-Service (MaaS) ARR surpassed RMB 16 billion. Concurrently, China Quick Commerce revenue surged 45% YoY to RMB 53.3 billion as order density improved unit economics, and International Digital Commerce (AIDC) narrowed operational losses. While aggressive AI hardware outlays (RMB 67.7 billion quarterly CapEx) drove quarterly FCF to -$6.58 billion (-RMB 44.7 billion), Alibaba maintains liquidity with cash and short-term investments of $66,363.6 million offset by $40,860.0 million in total debt, preserving net cash of $25,504 million ($10.56 per share).
what_changes_now:

On one hand, AI Cloud and Compute Services are demonstrating robust top-line momentum. External Cloud revenue growth accelerated to +45% YoY to RMB 48.44B ($7.14B) in the June 2026 quarter, driven by 12 consecutive quarters of triple-digit growth in AI-related products, which now operate at an annualized run-rate exceeding RMB 49.5B ($7.3B). On the other hand, the domestic commerce engine is bearing severe financial strain to defend transaction density across 1.0B active consumers and ~10M active merchants. Quick Commerce (Taobao Instant Commerce & Freshippo) surged +45% YoY to RMB 53.30B, but promotional campaigns and logistics subsidies continue to dilute consolidated profitability, holding gross margins at 34.0%.

Capital allocation has shifted decisively toward capital expenditures and liquidity preservation. Driven by server procurement and hyperscale data center construction, quarterly CapEx surged 75% YoY to RMB 67.68B ($9.98B), driving quarterly consolidated Free Cash Flow into a negative RMB 44.67B (-$6.58B) outflow. Management effectively paused open-market share repurchases ($162M spent in Q1 FY27 vs. $4.1B quarterly historically) and issued an HK$80B ($10.2B) ordinary share placement at HK$112.70 per share (~3.6% dilution) to fund its 3-year RMB 380B AI buildout program.

title: BABA: Valuation Re-evaluated (Narrow Moat)

In core e-commerce, Customer Management Revenue (CMR) yield on merchant advertising and software tools dropped 7% on a reported basis (+1% like-for-like), as spending shifts toward lower-AOV items and smaller marketplace sellers. Conversely, Cloud Intelligence Group external commercial revenue surged +45% YoY, powered by 12 consecutive quarters of triple-digit AI product growth and an annualized AI revenue run-rate exceeding RMB 49.5B ($7.3B). Cloud Adjusted EBITA margin reached 12.0%, demonstrating that standardized Model-as-a-Service (MaaS) workloads carry positive operating leverage.

Capital allocation has shifted completely. what_changes_now:
Alibaba operates a vast commercial digital ecosystem across mainland China and international markets. The business currently generates a real-time annualized revenue run-rate of $150,463.2M based on latest quarterly revenue of $37,615.8M (+8.6% YoY), supported by a consolidated gross margin of 38.2%. The current operational trajectory reflects a multi-speed structural shift. Legacy e-commerce Customer Management Revenue is experiencing minor unadjusted contraction (-7% YoY unadjusted / +1% like-for-like) as BABA reallocates user traffic toward Quick Commerce (Freshippo and Taobao Instant Commerce), which expanded +45% YoY to RMB 53.3 billion. In parallel, Cloud Intelligence Group is accelerating: external cloud revenue grew +45% YoY, driven by AI-related product revenue delivering triple-digit YoY growth for 12 consecutive quarters to reach an annualized run-rate of ~$7.3 billion (~35% of external cloud revenue).

However, funding this technological repositioning has significantly altered cash generation. Quarterly CapEx rose 75% YoY to $10.0 billion (RMB 67.7 billion), pushing quarterly Free Cash Flow into negative territory (-$6.58 billion). To maintain balance sheet liquidity for its 3-year RMB 380 billion ($53B+) AI/Cloud infrastructure roadmap without adding un-hedged debt, management temporarily paused share repurchases and executed an HK$80 billion ($10.2 billion) primary share placement in Hong Kong, diluting share count by ~3.7%.
